It works correctly, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher and exposes a narrow UsesResponsePlaceholders API there, coupling the packages the wrong way; tests are decent but there is only one handler-level test.

Production code is byte-identical to the reference, with good tests: the existing status-code retry test is parameterized with a direct ph() call, several request-only variants are added, and a Placeholders unit test includes a copy check.

Production code is essentially identical to the reference, and the table-driven tests are strong, covering method(), direct ph(), upstream.host, the similar name, the escaped literal, dynamic names and mixed matcher sets.

The retry fix itself is sound and well tested, but the patch also adds an unrelated DetachAfterHijack method to ResponseWriterWrapper, plus tests for it, which silently changes hijack-detach behavior for every embedding wrapper.

The fix is correct and follows the same approach as the reference: provision-time AST collection of ph() names plus a completeness flag, with the response-placeholder list kept in reverseproxy and thorough unit and handler tests covering every case maintainers listed; one minor nit is that it returns the internal slice instead of a clone.
